source_article_rows.article: Food product containing any of the above mentioned food articles
Sago, Cassava flour, Tapioca flour, Manihot flour and their products

records.source_basis: FSSAI CTR Version IX (03.02.2026), §2.2.1; current FSSR/FoSCoS identity

selectable_branches.label: Finished food may legally be a cereal product
positive_proof: Full ingredient recipe showing qualifying cereal content, not solely tapioca or other tuber-derived starch.
Official finished-article classification as 'cereal and cereal products', not a mere ingredient level match.
Complete analytical batch, operative regulation and correct FSSAI sampling basis.
selectable_branches.not_automatically_applicable: FSSR Chapter 2.4 listing alone does not prove the finished article falls within this CTR source when non-cereal base flours are permitted.

selectable_branches.label: Finished food may contain a listed cereal, nut, pulse, oilseed or spice
positive_proof: Quantified finished recipe and named commodity from the official CTR aflatoxin list.
Formal finished-product article classification and distinction from primary cereal/nut article.
Applicable processing, residue basis and laboratory records.
selectable_branches.not_automatically_applicable: The 20 µg/kg total-aflatoxin composite reference is NOT interchangeable with the 15 µg/kg cereal or nut reference.

selectable_branches.label: Finished article may be a cassava/tapioca/sago-flour product
positive_proof: Identify Manihot/tapioca-derived flour or sago product and finished-form standard with recipe evidence.
Prove CTR phrase 'and their products' applies to the finished formulated food, not merely any trace of modified starch.
Source-confirmed hydrocyanic acid method, sample matrix and laboratory evidence.
selectable_branches.not_automatically_applicable: Arrowroot, water chestnut, potato, maize and their starches are not automatically cassava/tapioca.

records.explicit_exclusion: FSSR cereal chapter scope does not establish a mandatory cereal recipe for all pasta, noodles or custard; papad, biscuits and Indian sweets may use non-cereal or mixed bases. Cereal 15 vs composite 20 µg/kg total aflatoxins must not be interchanged.
